items.statement: Within 6 months of referral to the clinic, at least 60 percent of eligible patients will be on at least half the target dose of every indicated medicine class, against about 29 percent in the June check.
items.rationale: Need and practice change are high because most patients are under-dosed; novelty is low by design, since the effect is established elsewhere; the measure uses the clinic list and needs no new data collection.
items.risks: Case mix of referred patients may differ from the June list; four-class titration may take longer than two-class titration in the trials.

items.statement: Offering telephone visits with community blood tests will keep missed visits in the most deprived fifth within 5 percentage points of the least deprived fifth.
items.rationale: A retrieved service report found the gap narrowed when telephone visits were added; the local population has similar deprivation.
items.risks: Small numbers per fifth in the first year; deprivation assigned by postcode.

items.statement: Potassium above 6.0 mmol/L will occur in no more than 3 percent of titrated patients.
items.rationale: Randomised and post-discharge series reported 2 to 3 percent; the protocol holds the antagonist above 5.5 mmol/L.
items.risks: Tests taken in primary care may be missed.

summary: Three service expectations; h1 is the main measure, h2 and h3 guard equity and safety.
